h1: GI in motion — what the ‘noise in motion’ actually is, and every lever measured
byline: Lane v3/gi-motion · 2026-08-11 · docs/internal/gi-motion.md has every number and how it was taken · M4 Max, Chrome / Metal · high = 1368×770 internal → 1777×1000 output, film grain off, the flickering tube held steady, unless a row says otherwise · levels = 8-bit output luma; ‘flow’ = the temporal sd of a world point followed through the pan
verdict: Verdict. On both shots of the recording the GI is not the term that moves. Removing the GI term outright (indirect scale 0, everything else identical) leaves the composite's flow under the pan where it was in every dark tile (GI share 0–1 % of the variance in the five clean tiles; 8 % on the panel-lit floor), and the built variants that act on the GI — B (GI denoised at internal res), C (young-history gather rays), D, and A's extra resolution — change no number past the take-to-take spread and nothing I can see in the crops. What moves is the direct chain under camera motion: switching ReSTIR back to the old leader / tail estimator takes 33–56 % of the flow out of the dark tiles and turns its 2–7-px blotches into ½-px grain, and switching off the resolve's motion terms (motion α 0.4, RCAS motion sharpen 0.3) another 10–20 %; the two together (‘floor’) land on the OLD renderer's numbers tile for tile (unlit floor 0.235 vs old 0.244 vs main 0.439 levels) — that pair IS the whole ‘v3 is noisier in motion than the old renderer’ in these tiles, while at rest v3 with the leader path is 20–40× calmer than either. On the static breach shot the wall's slow swim is ReSTIR's crawl too (GI 0 %), and there ReSTIR is the BETTER estimator (the leader path swims 2× more on the sun-and-sky wall).
verdict2: What I recommend, in this lane's remit (quality.ts rows / settings — an OPT-IN bundle for the designer's eye, not shipped as defaults): MOTION_CALM = ReSTIR's spatial reuse everywhere + the extra penumbra ray, and the resolve's motion terms halved (α 0.4 → 0.25, motion sharpen 0.3 → 0.15) — ?motioncalm, Tab ▸ Frame, __gimo.calm(): −14 … −24 % of the pan flow per clean tile at high, the STILL tiles −23 … −51 % (spatial reuse halves ReSTIR's static crawl too), the daylight wall +7 %, +0.79 ms union. The rest is not a row: reservoir reprojection that does not scramble lineages under sub-pixel camera motion, in restir.wgsl — another lane's file; §8 words it for that lane. Ship A (the climb) as the ladder feature it is (it works, and the same commit fixes ‘auto ↑’ on 60 Hz displays, where it never could fire); leave B / C / D in as identity-proven OFF rows that cost nothing off — no tier places them: on these shots they buy nothing at +0.85 / +0.65 ms.
scenes: Both scenes boot ?paused, reset the clock, seed Math.random, zero every anim.phase, park the guards dark, switch the storm and the film grain off and hold the fluorescent tubes steady at the start of EVERY take (a take renders the same jitter / dice sequence whatever ran before it in the page; the tube's occasional 14-Hz dropout bursts had put a whole-tile 16-level pumping into whichever early takes overlapped one). 24 consecutive OUTPUT frames are read back losslessly; each tile is a world rectangle sampled ≈ 1 output px apart and RE-PROJECTED every frame through that frame's own view-projection, so a point of floor is followed through the pan (bilinear luma). S1's follow camera pans 2.44 output px per frame at 1777 wide.
s1cap: S1 — the window-lit cubicle floor at night, Sam walking east under the follow camera (2.44 output px / frame). Tiles: unlit = the floor east of the light (L 32: 85 % distant direct light, 15 % bounce), unlitAisle, stripe / moonStripe (in the moonlit bands), lightEdge, litFloor (panel-lit, L 132), sillWall
s2cap: S2 — the breach stepped to the Stack shot: Blue One walking his last metre along the break-room wall, static camera, daylight. Tiles wall / wallHigh / door; his silhouette + 8 px masked per frame from the g-buffer's id target (coverage 0.475 of ‘wall’)
metricNote: Per tile: flow = temporal sd of luma per world sample, mean over the tile (levels; in brackets ÷ the tile's mean); |Δ| = mean frame-to-frame |difference| (≈ 1.13 × sd for white noise, ≪ sd for a slow crawl); boil = mean of (max − min) over the 24 frames; blotch size = autocorrelation half-width of each frame's residual along the tile's rows, output px. Repeats of main in one page agree to ±2 % (unlit), ±3 % (litFloor), ±8 % (stripe, a thin bright band); the ‘STILL’ column is the same tile with the camera pinned and Sam out of frame. Views: 0 = the composite; D = the composite with the GI term removed (indirect scale 0 — resolve, sharp direct, everything else identical: the GI's marginal share = 1 − varD/var0); 4 / 3 = the indirect-only / direct-only debug views (the terms naked — no resolve, no sharp direct — for attribution of the terms, not of the picture). Two more tiles placed inside the moonlit bands (‘stripe’, ‘moonStripe’) turned out to be occluded by the desk cluster's partition for part of the pan — the sampler follows the floor point with no depth test — and are out of every table; ‘lightEdge’, the boundary of the window light on the dark floor (a penumbra, the largest relative flow of all: 2.2 %), stands in for ‘the stripes’.
attr: The first table is the attribution the brief asked for, and it came out the other way: with the GI term gone the flow in the dark tiles does not drop (unlit 0.439 → 0.466, unlitAisle 0.531 → 0.528, lightEdge 1.589 → 1.673, sillWall 0.318 → 0.327, S2 wall 0.905 → 0.952 — slightly UP, the picture being darker); only the panel-lit floor (8 %) carries a measurable GI part. The GI term naked (view 4) does flow under the pan — 0.27–0.39 levels of ~30, blotch size ½ px, i.e. per-pixel grain the resolve then averages — but that is a term worth 4–9 levels of these tiles' 30–90; the direct term naked (view 3) flows 1.1–3.1 levels at 3–4-px blotch size in the same tiles. Third table: what the direct chain's own switches do to the COMPOSITE under the same pan.
attrAfter: Reading it: ReSTIR off (the leader / tail estimator) is the single biggest mover — unlit −33 %, the light's edge −56 %, litFloor −49 %, and the blotch size collapses from 2–7 px to ½–1 px; the resolve's motion terms off −19 / −14 / −7 %; the two together (‘floor’) = the old renderer's numbers. Why blotches pointed at the GI and were not: ReSTIR's per-pixel reservoir error is temporally persistent (M-capped history) and the shadow client's à-trous smears it 3–4 px; at rest that is a frozen faint pattern (the documented slow crawl — the STILL column: 0.19 levels vs the leader path's 0.005), under a pan the integer-pixel reservoir reprojection hands ~44 % of pixels a neighbour's reservoir every frame, lineages merge and split, and the frozen pattern becomes one that changes frame to frame at every world point — flow, at blotch scale, strongest where many dim lights compete for two reservoir slots (the ‘unlit’ floor is lit by a dozen distant panels). The leader path keeps no per-pixel state but a bilinear-reprojected ratio history: its error is white per frame and the resolve eats it. On the daylight wall (one sun + sky) the situation inverts: ReSTIR's reservoirs hold the sun and the leader path is the one that swims (S2 wall 1.84 vs 0.905).
knobs: Every A/B row the ReSTIR pass, the shadow client and the resolve already expose, one at a time under the S1 pan (the first evening's takes, film grain still on — it turned out to add under 3 % to these numbers, so they rank fine; four repeats of main bracket the spread). Winners: restirSpatialAll, restirPenRays (unlit −13 %, litFloor −10 %), restirHistory 20 → 4–8 (litFloor −24 … −41 % and the light's edge likewise — but see the STILL column and S2 in §3), taauMotionAlpha ↓ and taauSharpenMotion 0 (−12 % each in the dark tiles); losers: restirGradK 2 (+74 %), restirCoherent (×8), restirPermute, rays 5 / 6 (unlit −25 % but the moonlit band +25 %), dnShadowCap 6. The combinations c3 / c4 at the bottom are what §3 re-takes grain-free.
levers: The brief's variants, grain-free, beside the direct-side rows. A = more internal pixels (0.85 / 0.90 of the cap instead of 0.77; 1.0 would switch sharp direct off) or the gather at ½ instead of ⅓ res; B = the diffuse GI accumulated, variance-tracked and à-trous-filtered at the internal resolution (a guided upsample of the raw ⅓-res gather first; statistics still from the raw texels); C = 3× gather rays on texels with no usable history last frame (1–2 % of the grid under this pan, per-tile vote, capped 8 %); D = clamp-cut history length + young à-trous widening on the diffuse client; rSAP = spatial reuse everywhere + the penumbra ray; tOnly = motion α 0.25 + motion sharpen 0.15; MOTION_CALM (rSAPt) = both; rSAP10t / c4 = the same with the reservoir memory cut to 10 / 6; floor = ReSTIR off + the resolve's motion terms off.
leversAfter: A, B, C, B+C, D and their combinations sit inside the take-to-take spread of main in every composite tile of both shots (and B+C is main to three decimals even in the GI-only view under the pan: the residual it reshapes is under an 8-bit level there). MOTION_CALM takes 14–24 % out of every clean S1 tile AND halves the still tiles' crawl (unlit still 0.19 → 0.09, litFloor 0.16 → 0.08), the daylight wall +7 %. Cutting the reservoir memory as well (rSAP10t, c4) buys 3–6 % more in the dark tiles and 31–44 % at the light's edge — the penumbra, where a moving camera hurts visibility reuse most — but gives back half the still gain and costs the daylight wall +23 / +32 %: the row to revisit if the penumbra edges are what the eye catches. None of the rows reaches ‘floor’ (unlit 0.38 vs 0.24; light's edge 1.35 vs 0.53): the reservoir reprojection is the rest.
tiers: The same S1 pan (and S2 at ultra / medium / low) at every tier: the OLD renderer, main, MOTION_CALM, B + C (B alone at ultra, where C does not apply to the resampled gather), floor. Main gets noisier down the tiers (fewer pixels and rays per output pixel: unlit 0.42 ultra → 0.84 verylow) while the old renderer barely moves (0.24 → 0.28) — the gap the designer sees is widest on the cheap tiers. MOTION_CALM takes 10–36 % out at every tier; at low / verylow its ReSTIR pair puts the darkest tile's STILL crawl UP (0.29 → 0.38 / 0.44 — spatial reuse of 2–3-ray reservoirs trades its own noise in), so there the resolve terms alone are the safe half. B / C register nowhere but verylow (−7 / −13 %, inside its noise). GI's share of the variance: 0 % in every dark tile at every tier; 8–33 % on the panel-lit floor (most at low), 0 % on the breach wall.
maint: The designer's own window — 1024×1000 output at high, internal 788×770 (a 1229×1200-CSS pane at dpr 2): the same S1 take for main, the old renderer, the proposed rows and B+C. Fewer output pixels per metre of floor: every blotch is fewer pixels but the same fraction of the picture.
climb:
(A) is a ladder feature, not a noise fix: with GPU timestamps the ladder can see headroom the frame rate cannot (a machine presenting 60 fps with the GPU 9 ms busy sat at ×0.77 for ever). It climbs the scale in 0.05 steps to 0.95 (not 1.0: sharp direct needs the two rasters to differ), then the gather ⅓ → ½ and volumetrics ¼ → ½, ≥ 4 s apart after 3 roomy windows (rate ≥ 57 — under any display's refresh — AND union < 60 % of 16.7 ms); backs the newest rung off at once when the union passes 80 % or the rate dips right after a climb, everything off on a load spike, failed rungs held 60 s doubling; auto's ‘go up a preset’ — which could never fire on a 60 Hz display before (it asked for > 62 fps) — is now priced from the cost model at the next preset and held off after a hop that came straight back down. tools/qa/quality-plan.ts drives all of it (39 PASS). Below: what it does with THIS machine at the designer's window — the serialized calm-still union per rung, and the real ladder fed those numbers.

Measured here: ×0.77 (788×770) 7.1 ms · ×0.80 6.8 · ×0.85 7.0 · ×0.90 7.5 · ×0.95 (972×950) 8.0 · [×1.00 7.3 — sharp direct switches off there: not a rung] · gather ½ at the top 9.5. Fed those (+0.5 ms slack) at 60 fps the real ladder goes preset high (t 1 s) → 0.80 (6 s) → 0.85 (11) → 0.90 (16) → 0.95 (21) → gather ½ (26 s) and stays, nothing failed. In play the recording's frames were ~9 ms at ×0.77, not 7: scaled the same way ≈ 10 ms at ×0.95 — right at the 60 % band — so expect 0.90–0.95 with the gather at ⅓ in the office, the rungs handed back in the loud minute and re-earned after.
cost:
Serialized calm-still unions (each frame followed by queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()), interleaved A/B/A/B blocks of 12, medians; the designer was on the GPU for parts of the evening — pairs whose two A blocks disagree by more than 5 % were re-taken and the table says which are clean. Stress-minute p95 (QRF + rain + 8 smoke domains, __stress) for the recommended rows only.

Cross-build check (the same cubicles view on main @ 7b76e9e vs this tree with every new row off): gather 1.835 / 1.835 ms, temporal 0.262 / 0.262, direct 2.49 / 2.49, softblur 1.18 / 1.18, union 9.77 / 9.70 — the compiled-in B / C / D code costs nothing off. No stress-minute p95 was re-taken for MOTION_CALM: its +0.79 calm-still puts high's 13.6 at ~14.4 predicted (drop penRays first if the 14-ms bar must hold); image-quality.md's D2 (spatialAll alone) measured +0.5 ms in the stress minute.
reco:
• Per tier: keep C3j as merged everywhere; try ?motioncalm by eye — contact shadows under spatial reuse everywhere (image-quality.md's D2 measured them softer; the penumbra ray offsets part) and pan sharpness with α 0.25 (tjank.md raised it to 0.4 for that; the history de-blur stays on). If both pass: ultra / high / medium — all four rows into PRESETS (drop restirPenRays at high first if the 14-ms stress bar must hold); low / verylow — the two resolve terms only (free, −10 … −20 %), the ReSTIR pair after a second look (it raises the darkest tile's still crawl there).
  • A (ladderClimb): ship on. On this M4 Max at the designer's window it climbs 0.77 → 0.95 and the gather to ½ res on a calm still (§7) — in play, with heavier frames, it will sit a rung or two lower and back off in the loud minute, which is what it is for; and auto now goes UP a preset on a 60 Hz display.
  • B / C / D: in the tree, OFF at every tier (identity-proven, zero cost off). They are the tools for a shot whose flow IS the bounce (a torch swung across a wall in a dark room, the blackout) — not measured here, not the complaint. C's at-rest +0.5 ms wants its young test moved out of the ray kernel before any tier places it.
  • For the ReSTIR lane (restir.wgsl, not mine): the target is the ‘floor’ row — the leader path's motion numbers with ReSTIR's daylight numbers. Under camera motion reproject the temporal reservoir with a bilinear-STOCHASTIC pick among the 4 source pixels (lineages diffuse instead of merging / splitting in blocks), scale the M cap by (1 − k·|screen motion|) so a panning pixel leans on fresh candidates the resolve can average, and / or shade from the 2×2 reservoirs round the reprojected point while |motion| > ½ px. This instrument measures any of them in two minutes.
residuals: Residuals, said plainly. (1) Even with MOTION_CALM the unlit floor under a pan flows 0.38 levels where the old renderer flowed 0.24, and the light's edge 1.35 where old flowed 0.75 — faint 2–3-px mottling sliding under the floor and a busier penumbra edge when you look for them; the reservoir reprojection is the rest. (2) The daylight wall's slow swim (S2, 0.9 levels over 24 frames, whole-tile) is ReSTIR's crawl under a static camera plus the shadow client's occluder cue shortening the history round the walking man (−25 % without the cue, which exists for the trailing edge of a walking man's shadow — the shadow lane's trade); the bundle leaves it +7 %. (3) Luma only; chroma flow (the vending fronts) is not measured. (4) B's memory (+64 MB at high, ~133 at ultra) exists only while the row is on.
notdone: Not done, deliberately: no default changed on the direct estimator, the shadow client or the resolve (other lanes' files or the designer's by-eye calls — the numbers and the rows are here); no restir.wgsl work; B not tiered anywhere (the brief allowed ‘ultra only’ if over budget — it is under budget and buys nothing measurable, which is a stronger reason); the designer's exact GPU contention was not reproduced for cost (serialized takes instead); the froxel haze's own temporal behaviour under the pan was not separated (it sits inside ‘D’ = not GI, and the volumetric term in these tiles is small).
